body:
**QA run 2026-11-22 (round 2) - CamCraft v0.25.0 + SolidCraft v0.46.2** (Linux x86_64 tarballs; SolidCraft checked against its SHA256SUMS.txt, CamCraft against the GitHub asset sha256 digest)

Machines and agents: 7 headless agy jobs, model **gemini-4-neon-high** (Gemini only), at most 3 at once: q01-q05 on len, q06-q07 on skull. Each agent drove only `solidcraft-cli mcp --headless` and `camcraft-cli mcp`; agy ran from its own HOME so the pool's MCP config was not touched. Each job designed the part in SolidCraft, saved .sc + STEP, then did machine/stock/tools/operations, generate, verify and post in CamCraft, and wrote STEPS.log and REPORT.md. Every finding filed below was checked by hand on the same build (or read from the posted G-code) before filing.

| Part | Machine | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| q01 2D plate (rerun) | Tormach 770MX | 19 min | **posted**; round 1's #3019, #3021, #3022 hold; a spot-drill false gouge remains (#3451) |
| q02 3D mould core (rerun) | Tormach 770MX | 35 min | **not posted**: STEP and .sc refused (#3034, fixed on main after the tag); on the STL, adaptive refused "loop crosses itself" and three 3D Finish generates hung the server 21+ min (#3035) |
| q03 turned pin (rerun) | Tormach 15L Slant-PRO | 33 min | **posted** with a revolved-V thread model as a workaround; the part-off cuts 1.5 mm into the part (#3452, P1) |
| q04 V-carve sign + 2D pocket rest (new) | Tormach 24R | 46 min | **posted 5 of 6 ops**: rest machining cut only the corners (good); V-Carve is not in v0.25.0 (PR #3151 merged after the tag), so the engrave stand-in did not post; contour never cuts the plate free (#3443) |
| q05 4-axis indexed block (new) | Tormach 770MX + microARC 4 | 35 min | **not posted**: the agent never found the `tilt` field (#3449) and used re-clamp setups; 5-Axis Parallel generate took 17 min (#3035) |
| q06 wire die/punch + plasma bracket (new) | Sodick ALC400G, Tormach 1300PL | 31 min | **posted all three** after patching the Sodick machine (#3214) and setting taper 0.95° (#3210, fixed on main after the tag) |
| q07 MDF router bracket (new) | Sienci AltMill 4x4 | 30 min | **posted**; full-depth plunge on the first tabbed level (#3453), repeated tool changes (#3445) |

Filed (all `bug`, `source:qa`, `source:agent`):
- #3452 **P1**: lathe part-off puts the blade centre on the part end, a 3 mm blade cuts 1.5 mm into the part; verify passes
- #3443 P3: 2D Contour outside stops at Z 7.061 ("the part is solid below it") 3 mm outside the part, tabs dropped, status ok
- #3444 P3: STEP and .sc import refuse a plate with a hole on a pocket wall ("face 12 capped at 3.307 mm sag")
- #3445 P3: grblHAL post repeats M5 / T1 M6 between operations on the same tool
- #3446 P3: Tormach 24R: PathPilot post refuses Coolant Off, while Flood posts with no coolant word
- #3447 P3: setups kept in name order; a setup added second posts first
- #3448 P3: detect_holes puts a downward counterbore into a hidden `cross` list; generate refuses, edit_operation cannot clear it
- #3449 P3: list_operation_types lists only defaulted fields (tilt, rest, wire condition, plasma feed/pierce, enum values are invisible)
- #3450 P3: DXF import refuses an AC1015 file with a CLASSES section (SolidCraft's sketch.export_dxf writes one)
- #3451 P3: spot drill Ø8 90° 2 mm into a Ø5 hole still refused as a gouge (a case #3020's fix misses)
- #3453 P3: 2D Contour's first tabbed level moves the lead-in and plunges the full 18 mm into partly uncut sheet; verify passes
- #3456 P3: plasma tip-up warnings appear only inside gate.not_judged while findings and ok say clean
- #3454 P7: posted programs repeat the same G1 point on consecutive lines (534 of 1671 lines on the plasma part)
- #3455 P7: list_features closed-chain length leaves out the closing segment
- #3457 P7: lathe catalog tools have no tool material; TN-1600-0R8's 3000 rpm is above the 15L's 2500
- Comment on #3035 with the new hang timings (5-Axis Parallel 1040 s, 2D Contour 133 s, 3D Finish 21+ min).

Already known or fixed after the v0.25.0 tag (not re-filed): #3034 and #3210 (both fixed on main after the tag), #2898 (Circular rapids in stock, fixed after the tag), V-Carve (PR #3151, after the tag), wood cutting data (#3068, after the tag), #3124 (router files start on Flood), #3214 (Sodick ships no conditions), #3217 (wire listing), #2443 (G83), #3036 / #897 (catalog gaps), #1869 / #1870 (engrave and plasma on DXF chains not generated yet), #1531 (3D Finish takes ball nose only).

Not filed, for a maintainer's look: q03's profile turning approaches from behind the part end (Z -70.8, in the uncut bar) and feeds toward +Z with an orientation-2 insert; q07's whole-model outside contour with holes gives 89 XY crossings (picking the outer chain works); wire tabbed punch retraces the whole kerf back to the start hole with the cutting condition still on, and writes M00 twice; G76 refuses the default 29.5° flank infeed on Fanuc by design.

SolidCraft: nothing filed. Its volumes and areas were exact in every run; the q04 "SolidCraft" finding was CamCraft's tessellator (#3444). Minor notes only: `describe_command` takes `id` while `execute` takes `command`; `solid.loft` refuses an apex point with more than two sections ("not supported yet") and its docs do not say so.

Reports, STEPS.log, designs, projects and posted programs: [qa/round2-20261122](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/tree/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122) on the fork's `qa-artifacts` branch (`verify/` holds the minimal repros made while triaging). Briefs q04-q07 are new; they and the agy job script are on the QA hosts under `~/qa/` until #3435 moves the briefs into the repo.

## Run q01w: q01 2D plate on the Windows build, 2026-11-22 (CamCraft v0.25.0)

- **Machines:** Windows build on bacon (`camcraft-0.25.0-win-x64`, `camcraft-cli mcp`); Linux build on len (`camcraft-0.25.0-linux-x86_64`). Both run on the Tormach 770MX with the Tormach PathPilot post.
- **How it was driven:** one Python MCP driver and no AI agent. The same 50 tool calls with the same arguments went to both OSes; only the run-directory prefix and the path separator differ. The calls come from round 2's final q01 `.camproj`. The part is round 2's STEP and was not redesigned.
- **Windows, step by step:** every step was OK. That covers import, stock (+3 mm sides, +1 mm top), G54 at the top front-left corner, 7 tools, face, pocket with the island (the island stays standing), spot / 6.6 thru peck / 5.0 blind peck / M6 tap, contour with 4 tabs, chamfer, generate (8 ops OK), verify (`findings: []`, gate OK, gouge 0, rest 19.67 mm³ at the blind-hole drill tip), post (2352 lines) and save.
- **Extra Windows checks, all OK:**
  - Post, save, reopen and re-post into a directory with a space and `ü` in the path, plus `import_model` from that path.
  - Round 2's Linux `.camproj` opened and posted on Windows.
  - The `.camproj` saved on Windows opened and posted on Linux.

**Windows compared with Linux:**
- The posted `.nc` is **byte-identical** (`cmp`) on both OSes, and also identical to round 2's Linux `.nc`. The same holds for every re-post: unicode path, reopened project, round-2 project, and the cross-OS project.
- Line endings are LF on both (0 CR bytes). The Tormach post declares no CRLF.
- The verify findings, the `render_stock` statistics and image, and every other MCP reply are identical.
- The saved `.camproj` differs only in the model's `source.path` (the STEP's path on each OS). Round 2's project re-saved on each OS is byte-identical to the original.
- `tools/list` is identical. Server logs differ only in timings (Windows is about 3x faster).
- **One difference:** `detect_pockets` `min_corner_radius` is 1 ulp apart (Windows `2.4999999999998885` / `3.999999999996612`, Linux `2.499999999999889` / `3.999999999996611`). It does not change the G-code. This is the known platform-libm divergence, so I added it to #1010 as another instance and did not file a new issue.

**Issues filed:** none. The round-2 q01 findings behave the same on Windows, since the posted program is the same file. The q01 row in the table is unchanged.

**Files:** `qa/q01w-20261122T1446Z/` on the `qa-artifacts` branch of mkinney/Camcraft. It holds the STEPS.log, the driver and its call scripts, every MCP reply and stderr log for each OS, the `.nc` and `.camproj` from both OSes, and the STEP.
